subtitle: A Broken Kingdom, A Bitter Crown

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Chandra Shah silhouetted against a smouldering ruined fort and dark forested hills
panels.action: Chandra Shah stands wrapped in a plain cloak on a crumbling battlement, gaze hard on distant Mughal banners over the forests of Garha-Katanga, smoke and haze softening the broken skyline of old Gond forts.

dialogue.text: In the shadow of Akbar’s empire, Chandra Shah must choose: let Garha-Katanga vanish, or wear his father’s crown under another man’s seal.

i18n.hi: अकबर के साम्राज्य की छाया में, चंद्र शाह को चुनना है: गढ़ा-कटंगा मिटने दे, या पिता का ताज किसी और की मुहर के नीचे पहने।

panels.shot: wide aerial over dense Satpura forests, rivers glinting, tiny stone forts perched on ridges
panels.action: The camera soars above thick forests and winding rivers of Garha-Katanga, small stone forts clinging to ridges while distant plains fade toward Malwa and the Mughal heartland beyond.

dialogue.text: A few years earlier, these hills were a kingdom of their own. Garha-Katanga, forest and stone, ruled by the Gonds from old Chauragarh and Mandla.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही साल पहले, ये पहाड़ अपना राज थे। गढ़ा-कटंगा, जंगल और पत्थर का देश, पुराने चौरागढ़ और मंडला से गोंड राजाओं का राज।

panels.shot: somber wide of a ruined fortress courtyard, charred beams and toppled idols, with a faint Mughal camp visible beyond
panels.action: A devastated hill-fort courtyard lies quiet, charred beams and broken pillars scattered, a distant Mughal camp faintly visible on the plains below.

dialogue.text: Then came Asaf Khan from Malwa with Akbar’s farman, and the hill kingdom fell. Rani Durgavati died in battle, the fortresses were stormed, the palaces plundered.

i18n.hi: फिर मलवा से अकबर का फ़रमान लेकर आसफ़ ख़ान आया, और पहाड़ी राज्य गिर पड़ा। रानी दुर्गावती रण में मारी गईं, किले टूटे, महल लूटे गए।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Mughal field tent, Asaf Khan seated with chests and valuables around, scribes nearby
panels.action: Inside a rich field tent, Asaf Khan sits among opened chests, jewels and copper vessels stacked around, while clerks mark lists by lamplight.

dialogue.text: Abu’l Fazl records that Asaf Khan gathered vast wealth from Garha-Katanga’s stores. Too much, the emperor later judged, for a servant of the crown.

i18n.hi: अबुल फ़ज़्ल लिखता है कि आसफ़ ख़ान ने गढ़ा-कटंगा के ख़ज़ानों से बेहिसाब दौलत बटोरी। बाद में बादशाह ने इसे ताज के नौकर के लिए हद से ज़्यादा माना।

panels.shot: interior long shot of Akbar’s Diwan-i-Khas in Agra, Akbar on the throne, courtiers flanking, a letter being presented
panels.action: In the Diwan-i-Khas, Akbar sits on a low throne, nobles on either side, as a messenger kneels, holding up a sealed report from Malwa.

dialogue.text: In Agra, Akbar heard how his general handled the conquest. The Akbarnama hints at displeasure: the commander of Malwa had enriched himself from a frontier war.

i18n.hi: आगरा में अकबर ने सुना, उसकी फ़ौज ने ये फ़तह कैसे की। अकबरनामा इशारा करता है नाख़ुशी की तरफ़: मलवा का सूबेदार सरहद की जंग से खुद ही मालामाल हो गया था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Akbar leaning forward, one hand raised slightly, an official reading from a scroll
panels.action: Akbar leans forward, expression controlled yet sharp, as a court official reads aloud from a scroll listing the spoils and actions of Asaf Khan in Garha.

dialogue.text: Akbar punished Asaf Khan, stripping him of Malwa. But he still held the hill country. The question now: how to rule this broken land of forests and forts?

i18n.hi: अकबर ने आसफ़ ख़ान को सज़ा दी, मलवा छीन लिया। पर पहाड़ी इलाका उसके हाथ में ही रहा। अब सवाल ये था: जंगलों और किलों से भरे इस टूटे हुए देस पर राज कैसे चलेगा?

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandra Shah seated humbly in a dim side hall, with a few loyal retainers behind him
panels.action: In a shadowed hall with cracked plaster, Chandra Shah sits on a low mat, a simple turban on his head, a few worn Gond retainers standing at his back.

dialogue.text: Somewhere between these events, another figure stood in the ruins. Chandra Shah, son of Sangram Shah, half-brother of Dalpat Shah, a sidelined prince now surviving on the edges.

i18n.hi: इन सब के बीच, खंडहरों में एक और साया खड़ा था। चंद्र शाह, संग्राम शाह का बेटा, दलपत शाह का सौतेला भाई, दरकिनार किया गया राजकुमार जो अब किनारों पर जान बचा रहा था।

panels.shot: close-up on Chandra Shah’s face, lamplight catching the worry lines
panels.action: A close view shows Chandra Shah’s lined face in lamplight, brows drawn, as he stares down at a small worn signet ring in his hand.

dialogue.text: The Ramnagar inscription remembers him as the next ruler after Durgavati. But before he could rule, he had to wrestle with a harsher truth.

i18n.hi: रामनगर के शिलालेख में उसे दुर्गावती के बाद का शासक याद किया गया है। पर राज करने से पहले, उसे एक और कड़वी सच्चाई से भिड़ना था।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot of Chandra Shah with an elder advisor, seated on the floor over a rough map
panels.action: Chandra Shah and an elder advisor sit on the floor over a rough cloth map, small stones marking forts along the Narmada and in the hills, a few moved aside to the plains.

dialogue.text: He could not bring Durgavati back. He could not push the Mughal army out alone. But he could ask: was there a way to keep a Gond kingdom alive under new masters?

i18n.hi: वो दुर्गावती को वापस नहीं ला सकता था। अकेले मुग़ल फ़ौज को भी नहीं हटा सकता था। पर वो ये पूछ सकता था: क्या कोई रास्ता है कि गोंड राज नया मालिक मानकर भी ज़िंदा रहे?

panels.shot: wide shot of a Mughal frontier camp near Mandla, tents and watchtowers, with Chandra Shah approaching on horseback
panels.action: Outside a Mughal frontier camp with canvas tents and wooden watchtowers, Chandra Shah rides in on a small horse, flanked by a handful of attendants, as Mughal guards watch.

dialogue.text: Sometime after the conquest, Chandra Shah entered the Mughal orbit. The sources do not dwell on the meeting. Yet its outcome reshaped the hills.

i18n.hi: फ़तह के कुछ समय बाद, चंद्र शाह मुग़ल घेरे में आ गया। तवारीख़ इस मुलाक़ात पर ज़्यादा नहीं ठहरतीं। पर उसका नतीजा इन पहाड़ों की सूरत बदल गया।

panels.shot: medium shot at the edge of the camp, Mughal officer standing, Chandra Shah bowing slightly
panels.action: At the camp’s edge, a Mughal officer stands straight in quilted armour while Chandra Shah offers a respectful bow, his face composed but tense.

dialogue.speaker: chandra_shah
dialogue.text: If Garha must bow, let it bow and yet breathe.

i18n.hi: अगर गढ़ा को झुकना है, तो झुके… पर साँस भी ले।

panels.shot: medium interior of Akbar in consultation with a frontier noble, a map of Malwa and Garha between them
panels.action: Akbar sits with a senior noble over an unrolled map showing Malwa’s plains and the upland tracts of Garha-Katanga, his hand resting on the shaded hill zones.

dialogue.text: John Richards and others note Akbar’s pattern. In forested frontiers, direct rule was costly. Tributary chiefs, loyal yet local, made better buffers.

i18n.hi: जॉन रिचर्ड्स और दूसरे इतिहासकार अकबर की चाल गिनते हैं। जंगलों वाली सरहदों पर सीधी हुकूमत महँगी पड़ती थी। जागीरदार सरदार, वफ़ादार पर स्थानीय, बेहतर ढाल साबित होते थे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Chandra Shah in a Mughal administrative hall, receiving a robe of honour from an official
panels.action: Inside a modest Mughal hall, an official drapes a light robe of honour over Chandra Shah’s shoulders as onlookers watch, some nodding, others weighing him in silence.

dialogue.text: Under Akbar, Garha-Katanga did not vanish. Much of it was restored to Chandra Shah as a subordinate ruler. He received recognition, not as an equal king, but as a client under Mughal suzerainty.

i18n.hi: अकबर के दौर में गढ़ा-कटंगा गायब नहीं हुआ। उसका बड़ा हिस्सा चंद्र शाह को मातहत राजा बनाकर लौटा दिया गया। उसे मान्यता मिली, बराबर का बादशाह नहीं, बल्कि मुग़ल हकूमत के नीचे एक आश्रित हाकिम।

panels.shot: wide shot of a line of hill forts receding into the distance; foreground shows Chandra Shah and a Mughal officer overlooking them
panels.action: From a ridge, Chandra Shah and a Mughal officer look out over a chain of hill forts, some flying Gond banners, others already showing Mughal colours in the hazy distance.

dialogue.text: Later traditions speak of conditions: key forts and lands along the plains edge handed to the Malwa subah, the deeper hills left to Gond hands. The records are cautious, but the pattern fits Mughal frontier practice.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपराएँ कुछ शर्तों की बात करती हैं: मैदान की तरफ़ के किले और ज़मीनें मलवा सूबे के हवाले, और भीतर के पहाड़ गोंडों के हाथ। दस्तावेज़ सावधान हैं, पर ये ढाँचा मुग़ल सरहद की नीति से मेल खाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandra Shah handing over a symbolic key to a Mughal officer at the gate of a fort
panels.action: At the stone gate of a fort overlooking the Narmada, Chandra Shah extends a large iron key to a Mughal officer, villagers watching from the walls behind him.

dialogue.text: To hold something, he had to surrender something. Forts commanding routes to the plains likely passed from Gond to Mughal hands. Chandra Shah traded stone for time.

i18n.hi: कुछ थामने के लिए, उसे कुछ छोड़ना पड़ा। मैदान की राहों पर नज़र रखने वाले किले शायद गोंडों से मुग़लों के हाथ गए। चंद्र शाह ने पत्थर देकर वक़्त खरीदा।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Chandra Shah presiding over a small court in Ramnagar, seated on a modest throne
panels.action: In a newly built hall at Ramnagar, Chandra Shah sits on a modest carved seat, listening as petitioners from the forests bow, a drum and water pot placed beside his platform.

dialogue.text: From Ramnagar near Mandla, his line would later carve their story into stone. The genealogical inscription names him as ruler, proof that the Gond house still claimed a throne, even if its circle shrank.

i18n.hi: मंडला के पास रामनगर से, उसकी नस्ल ने बाद में अपनी कहानी पत्थर पर खोदी। वंशावली वाले शिलालेख में उसका नाम शासक के रूप में है—सबूत कि गोंड घराना अभी भी राज का दावा करता था, चाहे दायरा छोटा हो गया हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of a fortified village tank being repaired by villagers under Gond officers, Chandra Shah observing from a distance
panels.action: Villagers work to repair an earthen bund and stone-lined tank under the eye of Gond officers, while in the background Chandra Shah watches quietly from horseback.

dialogue.text: Under Mughal shadow, Gond rulers still dug tanks, guarded forests, and kept local order. The empire took tribute; the hill chiefs kept daily life from collapsing.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल साये के नीचे भी गोंड राजा तालाब खुदवाते, जंगलों की रखवाली करते, और इलाकाई बंदोबस्त संभाले रहते। साम्राज्य लगान लेता, पहाड़ी सरदार रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी को टूटने से बचाते।

panels.shot: close-up of Chandra Shah at night, sitting alone by a lamp, looking at a small idol and a Mughal-sanction document side by side
panels.action: At night, Chandra Shah sits by a flickering oil lamp, gazing at a small household idol and a rolled Mughal document placed side by side on the low table before him.

dialogue.text: No chronicle records his private doubts. Yet his choice is clear in the outcome: he accepted a world where Akbar’s seal and Gond gods shared the same house.

i18n.hi: किसी इतिहास में उसके मन की शंका नहीं लिखी। पर उसकी पसंद नतीजे में साफ़ दिखती है: उसने ऐसा जहाँन माना जहाँ अकबर की मुहर और गोंड देवता एक ही घर में रहते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot from behind Chandra Shah on a rampart, looking toward distant Mughal banners and beyond them the deep forests
panels.action: From behind, Chandra Shah stands on a rampart, one hand on the rough parapet, watching faint Mughal banners on the horizon while endless dark forests roll behind him.

dialogue.text: Chandra Shah’s bargain did not undo conquest or loss. It kept a wounded kingdom breathing, a Gond line ruling under another’s sky—a reminder that after ruin, survival itself can be a hard, deliberate act.

i18n.hi: चंद्र शाह की सौदेबाज़ी ने ना फ़तह मिटाई, ना खोया हुआ लौटाया। उसने बस एक घायल राज को ज़िंदा रखा—गोंड वंश को किसी और के आसमान तले राज करते हुए; याद दिलाते हुए कि बर्बादी के बाद, बचकर रहना भी एक सख़्त, सोची-समझी लड़ाई हो सकता है।

title_i18n.en: Chandra Shah Bargains After the Fall
title_i18n.hi: चंद्र शाह: पतन के बाद की सौदेबाज़ी

subtitle_i18n.en: A Broken Kingdom, A Bitter Crown
